name: 08-activity-driven-temporal
title: Activity-driven temporal network
question: What does an activity-driven contact sequence look like, where edges last only one time window?
hypothesis: With edges reset every step and nodes firing in proportion to their activity, each instantaneous graph is sparse and blinking, while the time-integrated degree follows the activity distribution.
objective: Run the activity_driven reaction and show how it reconfigures the network, measuring its signature structural observables.
description:
Activity-driven firing produces a sparse, blinking temporal network — each snapshot is instantaneous, unlike the accreting Family-A graphs.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `activity_driven` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
claim: Activity-driven firing produces a sparse, blinking temporal network — each snapshot is instantaneous, unlike the accreting Family-A graphs.

followup_proposals.title: Reaction–diffusion on a temporal (blinking) network
followup_proposals.motivation: Transport in Families B/C assumes persistent edges; activity-driven edges exist only for one window, so coupling should be intermittent.
followup_proposals.hypothesized_mechanism: Apply inter-node transport only across the edges present in the current activity-driven snapshot — intermittent, contact-gated diffusion.
